name: Drugmaxxing

card.summary: Using medications or substances to lower social anxiety and boost confidence and sociability, in the belief that a more outgoing presence improves how a person is perceived.
card.note: Involves prescription and controlled substances; forum members disagree about its value.

quick.overview:
Drugmaxxing is the forum term for using drugs or medications to optimise how one comes across, mostly by reducing social anxiety and inhibition. Proponents argue that a relaxed, outgoing manner raises perceived attractiveness and opens up a social life.

It is discussed alongside socialmaxxing, which means widening a social circle. Reports are anecdotal, and forum members themselves are split on whether it helps.
quick.how: Forum posts discuss prescription options such as SSRIs, benzodiazepines, phenibut and psychedelics for anxiety and sociability, and pair them with social tactics like many brief interactions. Members report mixed results.
quick.risks: Many of the substances discussed are prescription-only or controlled and carry dependence, side effects and legal risks. Some forum users report side effects or lack of benefit, and others advise building social experience instead. Medical supervision is the usual guidance for any prescribed drug.

lead: Drugmaxxing is looksmaxxing slang for using substances to optimise oneself, most often socially. Posters describe it as a route to lower inhibition and anxiety, so that they come across as more confident and likeable.[1][2]

A widely shared looksmax.org guide pairs it with socialmaxxing, defined as using compounds, protocols or tactics to expand a social circle and become better known, and presents it as aimed at neurodivergent users and people with social anxiety.[1] Another poster who reports being autistic said drugs made him low-inhibition and uncaring about others' opinions.[2]

Opinions differ. Posters report that SSRIs, phenibut or benzodiazepines helped some and not others, and some say psychedelics are the only acceptable option, while others argue drug use is not a good long-term strategy and recommend gradually building social experience.[2][3]

chain: Perceived as more confident and likeable
angle.text: Users aim to improve social presence, not physical features. The claim is that lower inhibition changes how they are perceived.

paras: The term covers any substance used to improve functioning, though forum discussion concentrates on anxiety, sociability and mood. Users share personal reports rather than studies.[1][2][3]

Supporters argue that for people with social anxiety or neurodivergence, compounds make social participation possible and that this builds popularity.[1] Others report relief from obsessive symptoms from prescribed medication.[2]

Some forum members report that benzodiazepines removed anxiety but also their wish to talk, and one argues drugmaxxing is not a good strategy long term.[3] Another reply suggests going outside and building social experiences.[3]
No studies found on drugmaxxing as a practice.

lore.intro: Drugmaxxing threads on looksmax.org mix experience reports and arguments over whether substances help.[1][2][3]

claims.claim: Compounds make socialising and popularity easier
claims.believers: A guide says compounds are a must for very neurodivergent users to branch out socially.[1]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested drugmaxxing for social outcomes.

claims.claim: Drugs can make you feel "NT" and uninhibited
claims.believers: A poster who is diagnosed autistic says drugs lowered his inhibition so he no longer cared what others thought.[2]
claims.experts: No published studies have examined this practice.
